key_insight: AI/ML can support nearly every stage of the ARPES workflow, from sample prep and data collection to analysis and theory comparison, but adoption depends on better shared datasets and reliable pretrained models.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials workflows, the paper highlights a path toward more automated, scalable, and reproducible ARPES experiments using AI-driven acquisition and analysis tools.
method: Surveyed ML methods relevant to condensed matter experimentalists
Mapped AI applications across the full ARPES workflow
Discussed a six-level framework for laboratory automation and self-driving ARPES
evidence_signal: The review notes that ARPES has multiple open databases, but they are still small and fragmented compared with large benchmark datasets like ImageNet.
watch_item: A major limitation is the lack of standardized, large-scale ARPES datasets, which can restrict model reliability, transferability, and validation.
paper_title: Progress and Prospect of AI in ARPES Workflow
